title: Graded degradation trigger misalignment and surge quarantine
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: On 2026-02-28 a multi-region traffic surge caused an SLO miss across two customer cohorts. The serving plane entered graded-degradation incorrectly: some nodes ramped into a degraded mode while others stayed in full-capacity, producing amplified retries and noisy tenant amplification. Circuit-breaker thresholds drifted due to skewed latency histograms; automated shedding did not isolate noisy tenants quickly enough. This ticket captures the post-incident analysis, root cause, mitigations applied during the event, and follow-up action items required to harden graded-degradation, CB hysteresis, and implement a ‘surge quarantine’ containment feature.
timeline: 2026-02-28T03:17Z - First SLO alert: trace-percentile 99.9 exceeded in us-west-2
2026-02-28T03:19Z - Traffic spike inbound from two high-throughput customers (tenant A, tenant B)
2026-02-28T03:23Z - Automated graded-degradation controller triggered on subset of nodes in us-west-2
2026-02-28T03:27Z - Remaining nodes did not transition (CB hysteresis mismatch), requests were redirected and retried
2026-02-28T03:35Z - Cross-region failover began to eu-west-1; KV-cache warmup lag noted on failover nodes
2026-02-28T03:41Z - Traffic shaping rules kicked in but retries amplified tail latency; manual quarantine applied to tenant B at 03:46
2026-02-28T04:05Z - Incident mitigated to acceptable SLOs after manual throttles and tenant B quarantine
2026-02-28T05:00Z - Post-incident conference call: immediate mitigations listed and temporary runbook edits applied
impact_summary: Duration: ~48 minutes of SLO degradation for a subset of customers. Customer-facing errors increased by 2.6x for the affected tenants. Platform-wide 99.9 latency rose from 340ms to 1.9s during peak. Two paying customers reported degraded functionality (one escalated to support). No data loss, no security breach. Estimated cost impact: elevated egress and extra compute (~$8k for the event window).
root_cause_analysis: Heterogeneous CB thresholds: circuit-breaker evaluation used 1-minute percentile aggregates on a per-host basis, but the graded-degradation controller used a separate 5-minute window. The mismatch allowed partial transitions and traffic fan-out.

Noisy-tenant amplification: high-throughput streaming tenants produced long KV-cache miss tails which caused per-token latency spikes; retries increased load and caused sibling hosts to see delayed CB triggers.
KV-cache warmup lag: cross-region failover nodes relied on cold KV caches; prefix-caching heuristic did not pre-warm top keys for heavy tenants during cross-region routing.
Insufficient tenant isolation: we lacked an automated ‘surge quarantine’ feature to temporarily cap per-tenant throughput during abnormal spikes without impacting global routing policies.
Observability blind spot: no high-fidelity tenant-level hysteresis metrics surfaced early enough; alarms triggered only after percentiles exceeded SLO windows.
Control-plane throttle: the control-plane decision propagation had 4–8s propagation variance across nodes; in the presence of retries that variance became significant for coordination
mitigations: Applied manual tenant quarantine to tenant B to cap concurrent requests and prevented further retries
Temporarily lowered CB sensitivity across us-west-2 to avoid split-state transitions (emergency config rollback applied at 03:50Z)
Added temporary KV-cache prefetch for top prefixes of affected tenants during the incident containment window
Updated runbook: immediate tenant-quiet/quarantine steps and escalation matrix added (runbook link below)

decisions: Short-term: enforce aligned aggregation windows between CB and degradation controller (P0) - accepted
Medium-term: build surge_quarantine as first-class policy attached to tenant metadata - accepted
Long-term: incorporate tenant-pattern-aware KV prefetch into routing layer - accepted with design review
follow_up_notes: Design doc for surge_quarantine should enumerate per-tenant billing/contract guards; product to vet per-customer actions before auto-blocking
SRE to own initial rollout of surge_quarantine behind a feature flag and dry-run for 2 weeks in staging
Telemetry team to instrument per-tenant retry amplification metric (ratio of retries to successful requests) and surface in alerting playbooks
Invite tenant-success and legal for any automation that can cap paying customer throughput; include checkbox in rollout checklist
